messages:
sara (AE): Heads-up — Cygnus Health just asked if we can onboard a bespoke model for their POC. They sent a short spec: 30B architecture, custom tokenizer, prefer int4 quant, must use customer KMS, SOC2 + data residency in eu-west-1. Asking for pricing for a 2-week POC and any compatibility blockers.

ana (AM): Thanks @sara — can you paste the model repo link? also need expected qps and latency SLO (p50/p95) for their app. 2-week POC usually = hosted trial + dedicated burst. Ballpark pricing depends on committed throughput. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sara (AE): Repo: https://git.example/cygnus/neo-30b-v2 (private). They said ~40 rps sustained, p95 < 250ms for simple chat completions. Will confirm datasets but they want to hit those numbers.

julian (ML Eng): quick scan: model uses RMSNorm + rotary embeddings and a nonstandard tokenizer (vocab ~130k). On runtime:
- RMSNorm: supported
- Rotary: supported but we need to validate kernel perf for long context
- Custom tokenizer: we can host tokenization in prefill pipeline but kv-cache keys depend on tokenizer id mapping — requires a short adapter during onboarding.

mason (Solutions Eng): For 40 rps @ p95 250ms, rough infra needs: 2 x A10G-like cards or 1xH100 depending on batch strategy. Memory: ~48GB working set if int4, ~60GB if we keep int8. If they insist on int4 quant, we should run an accuracy sweep — int4 can regress on generative quality for some models. Also need to confirm whether they want prefix caching enabled.

julian (ML Eng): Agreed. I can run a compatibility sweep. Need model weights and tokenizer in S3 (pre-signed) or we can mirror if legal ok. Sample runtime hint I want to try: 
```
model_config:
  name: cygnus-neo-30b-v2
  quant: int4
  kv_cache: enabled
  tokenize: external_adapter: true
  batch: {max_tokens: 1024, max_batch_size: 8}
  fallback_variant: redwood-compact-30b-quant
```
This will test perf/accuracy vs our redwood-compact fallback.

tess (Security): Important checklist items from security: KMS/HSM integration for customer keys (we support AWS KMS + BYOK in Private), network isolation (VPC peering or Private deployment), retention policy for logs, and EU data residency (we have eu-west-1 capacity but need contract addendum). Also they will want the security questionnaire filled — ask them to attach it. 

ana (AM): On pricing: for a short POC we usually offer a reduced Dedicated trial: ~$6k/week for baseline capacity (covers 40 rps target) + modest infra add-on if they want isolated hosts. If they go Dedicated production, monthly commit would be negotiated. This is ballpark — will confirm after the sweep. Can someone confirm if legal needs an addendum for EU residency?

mason (Solutions Eng): Legal/ops: yes, we need a DPA addendum for EU residency + possible SDS for logs retention. I can loop infra and contracts once they confirm POC scope. Also note: if we enable BYOK with their KMS, onboarding time + certs add ~3 business days.

sara (AE): Customer also flagged they will run an SOC2 Lite questionnaire first. @tess can you own initial answers? I can share their questionnaire doc.

tess (Security): I'll take it. Send doc to security@redwood.com. Quick note: for BYOK we need a key policy that allows our service principal; we'll provide an integration guide.

deploy-bot: Created POC ticket POC-1423 and linked workspace.

julian (ML Eng): Action: I’ll run compatibility sweep (perf + accuracy delta vs redwood-compact) — need access to weights/tokenizer. ETA 3 days. If int4 quality loss > 3% on validation prompts we should recommend int8.

ana (AM): Action: I’ll send the customer revised SOW: 2-week POC, includes one hosted reserved slot + fallback routing to redwood-compact if needed. Price draft: 
- POC fee: $12,000 (2 weeks) including infra and eng support
- BYOK integration: $1,500 one-time due to ops time
This is preliminary — will update after julian’s sweep and tess’s security review.

sara (AE): thanks everyone. I'll get the repo access and questionnaire from Cygnus and post here. Any other immediate blockers?

mason (Solutions Eng): Add-on: if they need embeddings/semantic search later, the tokenizer mismatch may require reindexing — flag for roadmap.

tess (Security): No blockers from security besides receiving the questionnaire and KMS policy.

julian (ML Eng): No infra blockers; waiting on artifacts.

ana (AM): Summary next steps:
1) @sara — get model weights + tokenizer + security questionnaire into POC-1423.
2) @julian — run compatibility sweep (3 days).
3) @tess — begin questionnaire answers and draft BYOK integration notes.
4) @mason — prepare infra estimate for int4 vs int8 (mem/cost).
5) @ana — draft SOW + provisional pricing (will update).

sara (AE): Copy — I'll post the artifacts into POC-1423 by EOD. :thumbsup:

ana (AM): Perfect — keep thread for any updates.
